You still have to click a tiny drop down to match manually and scroll an endless list to find the transaction.<br /> - There are no changes to the Reconcile feature.<br /> - One Step Update finally provides a status dialog which displays the status of the connections with the banks during the updates, of which I have five. For years I have paid my electric bill using a memorized category. Suddenly I have two different electric companies - one as a Payee, one as the old Category - and I have to use the Payee if I want to use online bill payment with my bank. (I don't know if it has always been this way - it could be the new bank?) This makes reporting a challenge. I still find the "renaming rules" completely confusing and thus unusable. Perhaps these would solve my problem?<br /> - The several files have been reduced to one. This might make backing up easier for some of you.<br /><br />The question Quicken wants millions of us to ask ourselves each year is -- is the $60 upgrade to 2011 worth it? Pluses: it is easier to use, it looks nicer and is a bit faster. Minuses: nothing substantively new, changes to the keyboard shortcuts, ads, it's $60 bucks. I said, Yes.

The thing about remote backups that you should seriously consider is this:<br /><br />Remote backups are a integral part of a sound backup plan. Businesses pay for remote backups (or storage of backups) because it makes the chances of loss much much less than one location backups. In fact, when I was working in IT and we lost our email server data file we were saved by having offsite backups. An offsite backup cannot accidently be thrown away or overwritten.<br /><br />Anyway, that is something to think about before dismissing online backups as a gimmick to get in your pocket.<br /><br />I have set up a non-stop backup job for my username folder to a second local hard drive. That seems to be working fine and restoring worked fine with my test file.<br /><br />I am getting a 2T external drive (the one I have is USB 1.0 and small) so I'll set up a disk image backup when I get that and update the review afterwards.<br /><br />I'm giving this 3 stars. I took a star off for price. There are some very nice free backup utilities so if you are going to charge $30+ it better be pretty awesome. I took off another star for having no apparent way to backup to some open format like zip or tar.<br /><br />Verdict - take some time to see what people are saying good and bad before spending your hard earned money on this software. For me, at least so far, I am satisfied with it.

The overwhelming reason for this is that there is not enough free space on your Kindle for the game to download and install. Even if the game successfully downloads, it has to install fully. If that doesn't work, try doing a hard reboot (hold the power button down for about 20 seconds), which will clear your RAM cache. My son has a first generation Kindle Fire, so I know it works on the Kindle. All your apps are stored on the cloud, and you can re-download them later. You might lose your saved games though, so keep that in mind.<br /><br />If you have a Kindle Fire with a larger drive, or if you're willing to uninstall nearly all your other apps, I promise this app works. Don't blame the developers, blame Amazon for not including a SD card slot on the Kindle Fire.

【正解】: 5 | 【予測】: 1 (1.2093288) | OOV: 71/700 | 【本文】: Elder Sign Omens is based on the cooperative roleplaying board game by Fantasy Flight Games of the same name (itself adapted from the more-complex Arkham Horror board game), and features the same art and gameplay from the board game, although some of the rules have been simplified. See the product description for a list of the differences between the app and the original board game.<br /><br />The art is worth the purchase price alone, and there is a fair amount of strategy, but most of the game comes down to luck as the gameplay involves using icons taken from the dice of the board game in order to match symbols and "solve" challenges. You have no control over which icons you get, although certain investigators have special abilities that can change the icons in some situations, and there are items (like clues and spells) that let you manipulate the icons. If you don't get the right icons to solve all the challenges in an area, you lose them one by one, and once you run out you take damage and likely cause some other bad thing to happen.<br /><br />Your goal is to lead a team of up to four investigators and collect a certain number of elder signs (magical symbols of protection) in order to keep a specific Great Old One (or Outer God in the case of Azathoth) from destroying the world. The base game comes with three campaigns (Yig, Tsathoggua, and Azathoth). You can buy 2 additional campaigns for $2.99 each that include new Great Old Ones, new gameplay mechanics, and new investigators. The Cthulhu campaign departs from the museum and has you exploring islands in the south Pacific in order to uncover R'lyeh and keep Cthulhu from awakening, while the Ithaqua campaign has you facing both the influence of the Great Old One, and the power of the weather as you trek across a frozen wasteland with finite supplies.<br /><br />Be warned that this is a hard game. There are several tutorial videos that show you the mechanics of the game, but even when you master the mechanics, gather a competent team of investigators, and use your items wisely, you're still going to die horribly more often than anything else. This will mostly be due to the high element of luck that's involved in the game due to its dice-based resolution mechanic. If you don't have the icons you need to resolve the challenge, you lose. It can be incredibly frustrating when you're doing everything you can, and the game is simply denying you the icons you need and causing you to fail over and over again. However, if you're patient, you'll eventually win.<br /><br />If you're a fan of the Cthulhu Mythos, H.P. Lovecraft, the Arkham Horror or Elder Sign games, or cooperative roleplaying board games in general, I would highly recommend this game. It's very difficult to find a group of people to play a complicated game like Arkham Horror or Elder Sign, not to mention that those board games (especially if you buy the expansions) are really expensive. This game allows you to challenge the Mythos solo whenever and wherever you want. I wish there were more campaigns, especially a "King in Yellow" or Nyarlathotep campaign, but those could be added later as expansions.<br /><br />The difficulty may turn some people off, so here are some tips for new players...<br />- Don't be afraid to use your starting items early. You get more items when you complete tasks<br />- Consider using 1 or 2 prime investigators to do the actual heavy lifting and using your other investigator slots for support characters (who can heal your prime(s)). This allows you to concentrate your items with 1 or 2 investigators, meaning that those investigators have access to more resources to tackle individual tasks.<br />- Remember your investigator's special abilities, and use the right investigator for the right task.<br /><br />Lastly, play the Yig campaign until you get the hang of the mechanics, and get better at planning and investigator management. Don't get frustrated when you lose (which you will ... a lot), and enjoy the wonderful artwork as you battle for your soul and sanity.
